notes: Dated project-maintained synthesis of the cited sources, not an upstream authority or live advisory feed. Verified affected-version mapping is limited to explicitly covered PHP 8.2-8.5 branches; do not extrapolate to unlisted branches.

CVE-2026-109618.title: PHP memory corruption during out-of-memory handling
CVE-2026-109618.unsupported_branch_notes: PHP <=8.1 is unsupported. No upstream fixed release is provided for these branches. PHP provides minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1; these are not upstream fixed releases. Vendor backports may exist and require vendor verification. This is not a verified affected range for older branches and establishes no lower affected-version bound.
CVE-2026-109618.sapi_notes: All PHP installations serving web requests are at risk: mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, LiteSpeed and FrankenPHP. PHP considers mod_php highest risk. SAPI alone does not establish safety or exploitability.
mitigations: Upgrade to the fixed release for the branch or a supported newer release; verify distribution backports with the vendor and restart workers.
Temporary measures reduce exposure but are not a complete fix. Isolate affected internet-facing services if patching cannot be completed.
At administrator level, consider memory_limit=-1 with container or cgroup availability limits. Allocation failures remain a risk; do not substitute RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA.
Set post_max_size to 8M without uploads or 32M when uploads are required; keep upload_max_filesize smaller. Apply decoded request-size and input-count limits at the proxy or web server.
verification: Confirm the PHP version of the web-serving runtime locally, not only the CLI or remote banner.
Check vendor security notices and installed package revisions for backported fixes.
Restart every serving worker after patching, then rescan the authorized endpoint; a banner alone cannot verify a backport.

CVE-2026-109619.title: PHP use-after-free through stale request-owned global state
CVE-2026-109619.unsupported_branch_notes: PHP <=8.1 is unsupported. No upstream fixed release is provided for these branches. PHP provides minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1; these are not upstream fixed releases. Vendor backports may exist and require vendor verification. This is not a verified affected range for older branches and establishes no lower affected-version bound.
CVE-2026-109619.sapi_notes: All PHP installations serving web requests are at risk: mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, LiteSpeed and FrankenPHP. PHP considers mod_php highest risk. A WAF or a different SAPI is not a substitute for patching.
mitigations: Upgrade to the fixed release for the branch or a supported newer release; verify distribution backports with the vendor and restart workers.

Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 before request parsing in php.ini, the FPM pool or server configuration; restart every worker. Do not rely on ini_set() or FPM .user.ini. This is partial mitigation only.
On PHP 8.5 set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart workers; this only mitigates the confirmed fatal-backtrace path.
Remove invalid or deprecated per-request settings that emit early diagnostics; remediate reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts. Hiding diagnostics does not mitigate the issue.
verification: Confirm the PHP version of the web-serving runtime locally, not only the CLI or remote banner.
Check vendor security notices and installed package revisions for backported fixes.
Restart every serving worker after patching, then rescan the authorized endpoint; a banner alone cannot verify a backport.

CVE-2026-115560.title: PHP configuration-dependent session upload progress issue
CVE-2026-115560.rating_notes: Project-supplied classification only: critical and CVSS v4.0 9.2 are not upstream ratings. PHP has no published upstream severity, CVSS rating or affected range for this CVE and has not published a full advisory as of generated_at.
CVE-2026-115560.condition: application sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize, then switches to php at runtime with ini_set() before session_start(), with session.upload_progress.enabled=1

affected.range: Not established by the informational advisory
affected.notes: Do not apply the fixed-version matrix for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to this issue.

CVE-2026-115560.sapi_notes: Requires the stated configuration and application behavior. A remote version or SAPI observation alone cannot confirm this condition.
mitigations: Apply the setting before request parsing and restart every worker until the next regular bugfix release. No out-of-band patch is planned.
verification: Inspect effective session.upload_progress.enabled and session.serialize_handler in the web-serving runtime locally.
Review application code for runtime session.serialize_handler switches before session_start(); remote version evidence does not establish this behavior.
Verify session.upload_progress.enabled=0 is applied before request parsing and restart every serving worker.
Check vendor updates and rescan the authorized endpoint for observations only; remote rescanning cannot confirm the local configuration condition.

mitigations: Only patching fully addresses CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619; temporary mitigations and WAF presence do not establish safety.
Disable session upload progress for CVE-2026-115560; the fixed releases for the first two CVEs do not establish remediation of the third.
